items.title: 8.3 The Binomial Theorem When the Index n is a Negative Integer or a Fraction (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 157-158: 8.3 Binomial Theorem when n is a negative integer or a fraction, binomial series (|x| < 1), Note box, Example 15, box of particular cases (i)-(vi) for n < 0

blocks.text: Ab tak binomial theorem sirf positive integer powers (1, 2, 3, ...) ke liye tha. Lekin science aur maths mein aksar aisi powers aati hain jaise \((1 + x)^{-1} = \frac{1}{1 + x}\) ya \((1 + x)^{1/2} = \sqrt{1 + x}\). Is sabaq mein hum dekhenge ke jab power negative integer ya fraction ho to expansion kaisi hoti hai. Achhi khabar yeh hai ke formula taqreeban wahi hai; bas do nayi shartein (conditions) yaad rakhni hain.

Jab \(n\) negative integer ya fraction ho, to
\[(1 + x)^{n} = 1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}x^{3} + \dots\]
\[+ \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}x^{r} + \dots\]
basharte ke (provided) \(|x| < 1\).
Is qism ki series \(1 + nx + \frac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2} + \frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}x^{3} + \dots\) ko binomial series kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan naya kya hai? Teen baatein dhyan se samajh lijiye:
1. Series kabhi khatam nahin hoti (infinite). Positive integer \(n\) par kisi coefficient mein factor \((n - n) = 0\) aa jata hai, us ke baad sab terms zero ho jati hain aur \(n + 1\) terms bachti hain. Lekin \(n = -1\) ya \(n = \frac{1}{2}\) par koi factor kabhi zero nahin hota, is liye terms be-shumar hain.
2. Shart \(|x| < 1\) bohat zaroori hai. Sirf tab hi terms chhoti se chhoti hoti jati hain aur jor ek khaas value par tik jata hai. Hamari taraf se misaal: \((1 + x)^{-1} = \frac{1}{1 + x}\). \(x = 0.1\) par \(1 - 0.1 + 0.01 - 0.001 + \dots \approx 0.909\), aur \(\frac{1}{1.1} = 0.909\dots\); bilkul sahi! Lekin \(x = 2\) par series \(1 - 2 + 4 - 8 + \dots\) kabhi kisi value par nahin tikti, halaan ke \(\frac{1}{3}\) mojood hai. Yani \(|x| \ge 1\) par formula jhoota jawab deta hai.
3. Bracket ki pehli term 1 honi chahiye. Formula \((1 + x)^{n}\) ke liye hai; \((4 - 3x)^{1/2}\) jaisi cheez ko pehle \(4^{1/2}\left(1 - \frac{3x}{4}\right)^{1/2}\) likhna parta hai, phir shart \(\left|\frac{3x}{4}\right| < 1\) banti hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text:
Is theorem ka proof is kitab ke daire se bahar hai.
Jab \(n\) negative integer ya fraction ho to \(\binom{n}{0}, \binom{n}{1}, \binom{n}{2}\) waghaira symbols be-maani (meaningless) hain.
Expansion ki general term yeh hai:
\[T_{r+1} = \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}x^{r}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Symbols be-maani kyun? \(\binom{n}{r} = \frac{n!}{r!\,(n-r)!}\) mein \(n!\) aata hai, aur \((-3)!\) ya \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)!\) is course mein define hi nahin. Factorial sirf \(0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\) ka hota hai.
Lekin product wali shakal \(\frac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}\) (jo 8.2.2 mein dekhi) mein sirf multiplication hai, jo kisi bhi number ke saath ho sakti hai. Isi liye general term isi shakal mein likhi jati hai.
Hamari taraf se misaal: \(n = \frac{1}{2}\), \(r = 2\): \(\frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2} - 1\right)}{2!} = \frac{\frac{1}{2}\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{2} = -\frac{1}{8}\). Yani \(\sqrt{1 + x} = 1 + \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{1}{8}x^{2} + \dots\)
Ab kitab ki misaal mein yahi general term \(n = -3\) ke liye simplify karte hain.

blocks.title: Example 15
blocks.problem: Find the general term in the expansion of \((1 + x)^{-3}\) when \(|x| < 1\).
steps:
Given: \((1 + x)^{-3}\), \(|x| < 1\); yani \(n = -3\).
To find: general term \(T_{r+1}\).
Method: \(T_{r+1} = \frac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}x^{r}\) mein \(n = -3\) rakhenge. Phir saare minus signs ek \((-1)^{r}\) mein ikatthe karenge, aur upar wale product ko factorial bana kar \(r!\) se kaatenge, taa ke jawab saaf aur chhota ho jaye.

Step 1: \(n = -3\) rakhein
\[T_{r+1} = \dfrac{(-3)(-4)(-5)\cdots(-3-r+1)}{r!}x^{r}\]
Kyun: factors \(n = -3\) se shuru ho kar har dafa 1 kam hote hain: \(-3, -4, -5, \dots\). Aakhri factor \(n - r + 1 = -3 - r + 1 = -(r + 2)\) hai. Kul \(r\) factors hain.

Step 2: Minus signs bahar nikaalein
\[= \dfrac{(-1)^{r}\cdot 3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5\cdots(r+2)}{r!}x^{r}\]
Kyun: \(r\) factors sab negative hain; har ek se \((-1)\) bahar nikaalein to \((-1)^{r}\) banta hai, aur andar \(3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5 \cdots (r+2)\) bachta hai.

Step 3: Factorial poora karein
\[= (-1)^{r}\dfrac{1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5\cdots(r+2)}{1 \cdot 2 \cdot r!}x^{r}\]
\[= (-1)^{r}\dfrac{r!\,(r+1)(r+2)}{2 \cdot r!}x^{r}\]
Kyun: \(3 \cdot 4 \cdots (r+2)\) mein shuru ke \(1 \cdot 2\) ghayab hain. Upar neeche dono ko \(1 \cdot 2\) se multiply kiya to upar \((r+2)!\) ban gaya, jise \(r!\,(r+1)(r+2)\) likh sakte hain. Is chaal ka maqsad sirf yeh hai ke \(r!\) kat sake.

Step 4: \(r!\) kaatein
\[T_{r+1} = (-1)^{r}\dfrac{(r+1)(r+2)}{2}x^{r}\]
Kyun: \(r!\) upar bhi hai aur neeche bhi.

Tasdeeq:
\(r = 0\): \(1\); \(r = 1\): \(-\frac{2 \cdot 3}{2}x = -3x\); \(r = 2\): \(\frac{3 \cdot 4}{2}x^{2} = 6x^{2}\); \(r = 3\): \(-10x^{3}\). Yani \((1 + x)^{-3} = 1 - 3x + 6x^{2} - 10x^{3} + \dots\), jo computer algebra ki series se bhi milti hai aur neeche box ke case (iii) se bhi.

blocks.text: Is misaal se do baatein seekhne wali hain. Pehli: negative \(n\) par saare factors negative hote hain, is liye un ke signs ko \((-1)^{r}\) mein samet lena sab se saaf tareeqa hai; isi se terms ke signs baari baari \(+, -, +, -\) aate hain. Doosri: jab upar lagataar barhte hue numbers ka product ho (\(3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5 \cdots\)), to ghayab shuruati numbers se multiply aur divide kar ke use factorial bana lena ek aam aur kaam ki chaal hai. Yahi chaal Exercise 8.3 mein bhi kai dafa lagegi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Fraction wali power ka ek chhota sa hisaab: \(\sqrt{1.1}\) ki qeemat. \(\sqrt{1 + x} = (1 + x)^{1/2}\) aur \(x = 0.1\), jo \(|x| < 1\) ki shart poori karta hai.
\[(1 + x)^{1/2} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}x - \dfrac{1}{8}x^{2} + \dots\]
\[\sqrt{1.1} \approx 1 + 0.05 - 0.00125 = 1.04875\]
Calculator se \(\sqrt{1.1} = 1.04881\dots\); sirf teen terms se teen decimal tak bilkul sahi jawab mil gaya. Yahi idea agle sabaq 8.3.1 (approximations) ki bunyaad hai.

blocks.title: Some particular cases of the expansion of (1 + x)^n, n < 0
Teaching note
blocks.text:
Cases (iv), (v), (vi) ko alag ratne ki zaroorat nahin: (i), (ii), (iii) mein \(x\) ki jagah \(-x\) likh dein, saare signs \(+\) ho jayenge. Case (iv) dar asal Unit 6 wali infinite geometric series hai jis ka common ratio \(x\) aur jor \(\frac{1}{1 - x}\) hai.
Coefficients ka pattern bhi dekhiye: power \(-1\) par 1, 1, 1, ...; power \(-2\) par 1, 2, 3, 4, ...; power \(-3\) par 1, 3, 6, 10, ... (triangular numbers). Yeh chhe cases yaad kar lijiye; 8.3.1 aur Exercise 8.3 mein baar baar kaam aayenge.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \((1 - x)^{-2}\) mein \(x^{9}\) ka coefficient kya hai? (Ishara: case (v) mein \((r+1)\), to jawab 10.) Aur \((1 + x)^{-1}\) mein \(x^{5}\) ka? (Jawab: \(-1\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Negative ya fractional \(n\) ke liye: \((1 + x)^{n} = 1 + nx + \frac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2} + \dots\), infinite series, sirf \(|x| < 1\) par sahi.
2. Bracket ki pehli term 1 honi chahiye.
3. General term: \(T_{r+1} = \frac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}x^{r}\); yahan \(\binom{n}{r}\) istemal na karein.
4. \((1 + x)^{-3}\) ki general term \((-1)^{r}\frac{(r+1)(r+2)}{2}x^{r}\) hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Series ko \(n + 1\) terms par rok dena: \(n = -2\) par terms be-shumar hain, "\(-1\)" terms ka koi matlab nahin.
2. Shart \(|x| < 1\) (ya \(|2x| < 1\) waghaira) likhna bhool jana; exam mein is ke number katte hain.
3. \(\binom{-3}{r}\) ko factorial se nikaalne ki koshish: \((-3)!\) be-maani hai.
4. Minus signs gum kar dena: \(n = -3\) par \(n(n-1) = (-3)(-4) = 12\), positive hai.
